current_attestor.observed_filter_semantics: Only /proc/<pid>/maps pathnames whose basename contains libsqlite3.so enter the SQLite mapping identity set.
current_attestor.nonclaim: The attestor does not claim productive Frank persistence-path exercise or Frank identity.

fresh_repo_evidence.result: Receipt-tail SQLite mapping is re-sampled after process metadata and same-generation mapping change fails closed.
PID plus process start ticks does not uniquely identify executable image across same-PID execve; exact tested Python-to-sleep treatment is already closed by merged PR 545.
Earlier same-source-id renamed-provider preload interposition falsified a weaker V1 admission claim; later guards added loader-environment/provider checks.

external_primary_evidence.fact: The WAL-reset corruption bug affects SQLite through 3.51.2 and is fixed in 3.51.3 and later; trigger requires WAL plus concurrent connections and concurrent write/checkpoint timing.
3.53.4 descends from the fixed 3.53 line and reports source id 2026-07-24 19:02:57 bf7c7f30031888f4e796e429ab3978879485813aaca6f641c7b33e4e09459bcc.
/proc/PID/maps describes currently mapped memory regions with pathname/device/inode information; mapping presence is not itself an attribution of application call-path ownership.
sqlite3.sqlite_version reports the runtime SQLite library version used by the Python sqlite3 module.

grf.observed_anchor: Current live attestor strongly fences one expected libsqlite3 mapping identity but intentionally has narrower scope than productive persistence-path/provider identity.
grf.generated_reality: If the productive Frank DB call path is necessarily bound to the attested expected SQLite object, current mapping attestation plus a real persistence-path exercise can close the remaining storage-runtime identity gap.
grf.counter_reality: A process can retain the expected attested libsqlite3 mapping while a differently named second SQLite-API provider is also mapped; filename-filtered mapping identity alone cannot prove which provider a productive DB operation actually used.
grf.falsifier: Bind a real productive Frank persistence operation to provider identity from inside the actual SQLite call path, then require exact match to the root-anchored 3.53.4 object across restart and rollback/downgrade tests.

unusual_experiment.name: POST_ADMISSION_RENAMED_PROVIDER_MAPPING
unusual_experiment.setup: A disposable C loader process dlopen()ed a tiny expected DSO named libsqlite3.so.0 exporting sqlite3_libversion, then treatment additionally dlopen()ed a second tiny provider exporting the same API under basename frank_shadow_provider.so. No database was opened.
unusual_experiment.claim_boundary: This does not demonstrate a Frank exploit, does not bypass V5/V6 startup guards, and does not show that Frank currently calls an alternate provider. It only proves that the current live-attestor pathname filter cannot by itself establish closure over differently named SQLite-API providers.
unusual_experiment.rollback: Temporary files/processes only; process terminated and temporary directory removed.

recommended_next_falsifier.name: PRODUCTIVE_SQLITE_CALLPATH_PROVIDER_ATTESTATION
requirements: Exercise the exact productive Frank persistence path on the accepted Ubuntu lane.
Record sqlite3.sqlite_version and SQLite source id from that same runtime path.
Bind the provider used by the actual DB call path to the root-anchored DSO identity rather than inferring from a matching mapping elsewhere in the process.
Require exact device/inode/hash/source-id continuity before and after the operation.
Repeat after clean restart and under downgrade/library-swap negative controls.
Fail closed if provider attribution is unknown, divergent, stale, or cannot be reconciled.
